record.summary: Comprehensive federal order on AI safety and security. Under the Defense Production Act it directed the Secretary of Commerce to require companies developing potential dual-use foundation models to report on training, model-weight security and the results of red-team testing, with interim thresholds of 10^26 operations (10^23 for models trained mainly on biological sequence data) and for large computing clusters. It tasked NIST with guidelines and benchmarks for AI safety, red-teaming and evaluation, and directed agency action on synthetic-content labelling, critical infrastructure and cybersecurity, chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks, and federal use of AI.

verification.note: Stored on 16 Oct 2026 from govinfo.gov (Government Publishing Office): the Federal Register printing of EO 14110 (Vol. 88, No. 210, 1 Nov 2023, pp. 75191-75226, FR Doc. 2023-24283), which gives the title, the number, the signing on 30 Oct 2023 and the provisions summarised; and the Federal Register text of EO 14148 of 20 Jan 2025 (FR Doc. 2025-01901), whose section 2 lists EO 14110 among the orders revoked. federalregister.gov has answered the archiver only with a bot-check page since 11 Oct 2026, so official_url now points at the govinfo.gov copy of the same Federal Register issue. The statements in notes on EO 14179 and on the fate of the implementing instruments rest on the records US-11, US-05, US-06 and US-09, not on files stored for this record.

judgment.status_reasoning: EO 14148 of 20 Jan 2025 (Federal Register of 28 Jan 2025, FR Doc. 2025-01901), section 2, revokes a list of orders that includes '(ggg) Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023'. So 'Revoked / withdrawn' stands, with date_last_updated 2025-01-20, the date of the revoking order. The order took effect on signature: it states no other date, and the signature line reads 'THE WHITE HOUSE, October 30, 2023.'
